chunks: The Hakim, Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali in Balkh informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id narrated to me, saying: Abu Na'im narrated to us, saying: Isam ibn Qudama narrated to us, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family).

That he said to his wives: I wish I knew which one of you is the companion of the camel 'al-adbab', whom the dogs of Haw'ab will bark at, and many will be killed on her right and on her left, and then she will be saved after she was near (to perishing).
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'camel al-adbab' and 'dogs of Haw'ab' in this hadith from Maani al-Akhbar?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* identifies Aisha as the 'companion of the camel al-adbab,' linking her to the Battle of the Camel where she faced the 'dogs of Haw'ab' (her supporters) and emerged victorious despite near-defeat. The term 'al-adbab' (the bridled or harnessed) signifies her role as the central figure of the conflict, while the 'dogs barking' metaphorically represents the clamor of her faction. This narration is pivotal in Shia exegesis for establishing Aisha’s specific historical and theological status regarding the early caliphate disputes.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were informed by al-Hakim, Abu Hamid, Ahmad bin Hussain bin Ali, in Balkh, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Abbas, that he said: We were told by Ibrahim bin Ishaq, that he said: I was told by Ibrahim bin Sa’eed, that he said: We were told by Abu Na’eem, that he said: We were told by Isam bin Qudama, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family,

that he said to his women: I wish I knew which one of you is going to be one with the camel that is adbab to whom the dogs of Haw’ab, and then, it will be killed, by her right and by her left, many victims, and then she will be saved after she is near.
